The tests failures look legitimate and seem to be tied to this PR after combining the queries. I'm not too familiar with the tests, but it'd probably be worth investigating if merging is the desired behavior.

```
/home/prow/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/_output/local/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/kubectl/kubectl.go:388
Mar 11 18:01:48.961: Unexpected kubectl exec output. Wanted "running in container", got "running in container echo running in container"
```

@Jefftree yeah, I definitely broke those tests, they fail when I run them locally too.  I'll take a look at it again and see if I can figure out what is going on.  Its been a long time since I originally worked on this, so I will need to regain my context and how to reproduce the issue so I can properly test the fix.

I'm still looking into this, but I made a comment on the original issue with how I am able to reproduce the issue locally 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/89360#issuecomment-797207790

I'm going back to what I originally had :sweat_smile:  .  I think it is the only safe way to handle it.  

Merging the query strings worked for proxy, but broke exec, which broke a bunch of e2e tests as you saw.

Running the tests locally, I can see the problem seems to be that it is duplicating the parameters for exec.   Example below from kubelet.log when I ran one of the failing e2e tests:

Current release version of code (with none of my changes). This is when the test passed. You can see exec has `command=cat&command=/etc/hosts/`
```
I0311 22:41:36.516313  522022 httplog.go:89] "HTTP" verb="POST" URI="/exec/e2e-kubelet-etc-hosts-794/test-pod/busybox-1?command=cat&command=%2Fetc%2Fhosts&error=1&output=1" latency="97.498713ms" userAgent="e2e.test/v1.21.0 (linux/amd64) kubernetes/8a1f30a -- [sig-node] KubeletManagedEtcHosts should test kubelet managed /etc/hosts file [LinuxOnly] [NodeConformance] [Conformance]" srcIP="127.0.0.1:50428" hijacked=true
```

After my previous attempt to merge the location and request query strings, it duplicated the commands and added a whole bunch more keys that exec doesn't want. This is when the same e2e test failed:
```
I0311 22:32:41.988978  504654 httplog.go:89] "HTTP" verb="POST" URI="/exec/e2e-kubelet-etc-hosts-8088/test-pod/busybox-1?command=cat&command=%2Fetc%2Fhosts&command=cat&command=%2Fetc%2Fhosts&container=busybox-1&container=busybox-1&error=1&output=1&stderr=true&stdout=true" latency="102.314984ms" userAgent="e2e.test/v1.21.0 (linux/amd64) kubernetes/8a1f30a -- [sig-node] KubeletManagedEtcHosts should test kubelet managed /etc/hosts file [LinuxOnly] [NodeConformance] [Conformance]" srcIP="127.0.0.1:48856" hijacked=true
```

So bottom line (I think) is fixing the query string for proxy is breaking it for other things that rely on the query string to work, like exec.

---

With this PR as it stands currently, it has a safeguard in that it will not alter the query string if the location has a query string.  So in the case of exec, it will be safe.  And I believe in the case of proxy this also fixes the problem.  So I think this would be an improvement.  But I am open to other suggestions or ideas if someone else knows of a more comprehensive way to handle merging the query strings in a way that won't break exec.

issue_context.title: Kubectl proxy would strip out the parameter for websocket request
issue_context.body:
**What happened**:
Create a deployment to run a websocket server. Use `kubectl proxy` for accessing the service outside of the cluster.

**What you expected to happen**:

Invoke the URL, for example as below, would pas in the token to the websocket server.
```
"ws://..../api/v1/namespaces/..../services/theservice/proxy/websocket?token=123"
```

However, instead, the parameter is stripped out.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52658745/77302773-ce93c200-6d2c-11ea-9d94-c1f085ef5215.png)


**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.17.1
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): Darwin
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): Darwin Kernel Version 19.2.0:
- Install tools:
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:

I know this issue is closed, but some people might still be interested in it.  For the record, I believe these two examples illustrate the problem and show how to reproduce it...

# SCENARIO 1: kubectl port-forward (Working as expected)

Terminal 1:
```
$ k run ws --image=brianpursley/hello-websocket-server
pod/ws created
$ k logs ws -f
Server listening on port 8888
```

Terminal 2:
```
$ k port-forward ws 8888
Forwarding from 127.0.0.1:8888 -> 8888
Forwarding from [::1]:8888 -> 8888
```

Terminal 3:
```
$ wscat -c ws://localhost:8888?foo=bar
Connected (press CTRL+C to quit)
> 
```

Output from Terminal 1.  Notice it shows the query string `?foo=bar`. This seems fine:
```
New connection with path /?foo=bar and headers:
{
  'sec-websocket-version': '13',
  'sec-websocket-key': 'mSworLWncMDgONfCQLXutw==',
  connection: 'Upgrade',
  upgrade: 'websocket',
  'sec-websocket-extensions': 'permessage-deflate; client_max_window_bits',
  host: 'localhost:8888'
}
```



# SCENARIO 2: kubectl proxy (Dropping query string)

Terminal 1:
```
$ k run ws --image=brianpursley/hello-websocket-server
pod/ws created
$ k logs ws -f
Server listening on port 8888
```

Terminal 2:
```
$ k proxy
Starting to serve on 127.0.0.1:8001
```

Terminal 3:
```
$ wscat -c ws://localhost:8001/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods/ws:8888/proxy?foo=bar
Connected (press CTRL+C to quit)
> 
```

Output in Terminal 1. **Notice the path does not include the query string (`?foo=bar`)**. It was dropped:
```
New connection with path / and headers:
{
  host: 'localhost:8001',
  'user-agent': 'kubectl/v1.19.2 (linux/amd64) kubernetes/f574309',
  connection: 'Upgrade',
  'sec-websocket-extensions': 'permessage-deflate; client_max_window_bits',
  'sec-websocket-key': 'R9n/qiVwdaBwlNUZ98vUtA==',
  'sec-websocket-version': '13',
  upgrade: 'websocket',
  'x-forwarded-for': '127.0.0.1, 127.0.0.1'
}
```
/cc @brianpursley I submitted a PR(https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120290) to fix this, you can take a look when you have time :)
